note: One short explanation per unfamiliar word, the same in CCS Console Workbench (standalone and inside Classic Cart Studio for Windows) and on the Classic Cart Studio website. Forms: the exact words matched in a sentence (case matters; a plural s is matched too). Scope page: explained once on a page (the product names), otherwise once in each block of text. Text: the meaning, the same for every console. Detail: what is particular to the consoles this version knows, named as such (it may differ on another console).

terms.text: Classic Cart Studio, CCS for short, is a free app for building and playing collections of NES games, on classiccartstudio.com and as an app for Windows. CCS HOME is the game-selection screen it makes for a console. CCS Console Workbench, its tool for backing up, restoring and repairing a console, is part of the Windows app and also comes as a standalone program that works on its own.

Classic Cart Studio's tool for a console's backups: back up, restore, repair and compose. It is part of Classic Cart Studio for Windows and also comes as a standalone program that works without the full app. In this preview version, connecting to a real console is not available yet; backups already on a PC can be browsed, checked and repaired.
terms.detail: Consoles to choose from at the top of its window: the NES Classic Mini and the SNES Classic Mini. In this preview, its console tasks are written for the NES Classic Mini; those for the SNES Classic Mini are being built.

terms.text: The game-selection screen Classic Cart Studio makes for a console, in one of four themes. It is separate from the console's original menu, which stays. You can preview it on a PC; putting it on a console is not available in this preview version yet.
terms.detail: This version makes CCS HOME for the NES Classic Mini.

terms.text: An installation option that adds a chooser for CCS HOME and other system software you set up on the console. It uses Hakchi2 CE underneath. Setting it up changes the console, and any other system software must come from you and is checked before it is offered.

terms.tech: the hakchi package ccs-mod (CCS Mod for Hakchi)
terms.text: An installation option that adds CCS HOME as an entry in the console's own menu, using Hakchi2 CE underneath. The console still starts in its own menu unless you choose to open CCS HOME when it is turned on. Setting it up changes the console.
The free community project that lets people add games and software to these consoles. Classic Cart Studio uses parts of its version 3.9.3, and CCS Mod and CCS Nucleus run on top of it.

A special way of starting a console so that it waits for a connected PC instead of starting its normal software, used to recover a console and to run tools on it. How to start it depends on the console: Workbench's connection steps say how for the console you chose. Nothing on the console changes just by being in this mode. In this preview version, connecting to a real console is not available yet.
terms.detail: NES and SNES Classic Mini: the USB mode of the console's chip (FEL).

terms.text: The console's startup image: the operating system's start-up software that the bootloader loads, which then starts everything else. Preparing a console replaces it, a change you review in Developer Mode can, and a restore puts back the console's own copy from its backup.
terms.detail: NES and SNES Classic Mini: a boot image holding a Linux kernel and its start-up files.

terms.text: The small programs a console runs first when it is turned on. They prepare the console and then load and start its startup software. Console Rescue is the Workbench task for repairing them from this console's own backup.
terms.detail: NES and SNES Classic Mini: two stages, boot0 and boot1 (U-Boot).

terms.text: A console's system software (its own programs and built-in games) as one file. CCS Nucleus can add system images you supply as choices; Workbench checks each one first. A system image is not startup software, and one console's system image is not automatically right for another.
terms.detail: NES and SNES Classic Mini: a SquashFS file system image (.hsqs).

terms.text: The storage built into a console that keeps its software and data: its startup software, its system, games, saves and settings. A console backup copies all of it. Games on a USB drive or SD card are not in it.
terms.detail: NES and SNES Classic Mini: NAND flash memory.

terms.text: A game's own save, the kind an original cartridge kept with a battery: your progress, kept by the game itself.
terms.detail: NES Classic Mini: cartridge.sram, or save.sram for games added with hakchi. Workbench's save conversion is for NES games.

terms.text: A snapshot of a game at one moment, made when you suspend it from the console's menu, so you can continue from exactly there. It is not the game's own battery save.
terms.detail: NES Classic Mini: suspendpoint1 to suspendpoint4 (*.state files).

terms.text: In Expert Mode and Developer Mode: a backup of this console you choose as the dated point you can go back to. Changes made after that backup are not in it.
Reading a backup file back in full and comparing every part with its checksums. A passed check means the file is intact; it is not a test of restoring it.
Extra data Backup Repair can make beside a backup file, so that a later small damage to the file can be repaired. It is not a second copy.
The time a console task is connected to the console. Workbench identifies a console only in a task's own session; an earlier session's console is shown apart, marked earlier.
A complete copy of one console's built-in storage, made by Back Up Console (a .zip file). Restore puts it back on that same console.
A collection or full Studio backup made in the Classic Cart Studio app (a .ccs file), with its game files. It is not a console backup and is not used here.
A battery save converted from a backup for Classic Cart Studio's player, with a report beside it. The backup itself is never changed.
Pictures and appearance settings for CCS HOME, made in HOME Designer (a .ccshome file). No games, saves or console files.
A plan from Console Composer (a .ccsplan file): the choices for a setup, with no game files, saves or private console details. It never changes a console by itself.
Built by Console Composer for one console (a .zip file): the files to put on that console. It holds your own files, so keep it private.
